subject: Taxes
title: How Tax Brackets Work
description: A quick win: understand How Tax Brackets Work.

hook.text: Moving to a higher tax bracket doesn't mean all your income is taxed at the higher rate.

buildup.text: The US has seven tax brackets: 10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, and 37%. Each applies to a specific income range.

discovery.text: If you earn $50,000, you pay 10% on the first $11,000, 12% on the next $33,725, and 22% on the rest. It's layered.

twist.text: Many people turn down raises fearing a higher bracket. But they'd still take home more money.

climax.text: Tax brackets are like stairs—you only pay the higher rate on income above each step, not on everything below it.

punchline.text: Higher bracket? Only the top slice pays more. The rest stays low.

quiz.question: If you move into a higher tax bracket, what is taxed at the new rate?
options: Only the income above the bracket threshold
